script: Spread and total were not saved, so this script is form-only: JAX should stay balanced because Bhayshul Tuten has 43 carries for 204 yards and Cincinnati has allowed 5.00 YPC with 8 runs of 10+, while Trevor Lawrence is +0.45 EPA/dropback with no blitz and Cincinnati blitzes only 14%. Cincinnati's grind is capped by a Jacksonville front allowing 3.79 YPC, so Joe Burrow (facing a 32% blitz where he is -0.31 EPA) has to find explosives rather than lean on Chase Brown's 49 carries for 197 yards.
who_goes_off: Bhayshul Tuten should go off on the ground at 4.74 YPC on 43 carries into a Cincinnati defense allowing 5.00 YPC, and Tee Higgins should go off through the air after 244 yards and 302 air yards on 23 targets against a Jacksonville secondary that has allowed 13 passes of 20+ on 92 attempts.
weak_spot: Cincinnati's real leak is the run front (5.00 YPC, 8 runs of 10+) plus the middle and left (9.23 YPA on 30 middle attempts, 8.43 on 37 left) while the right side holds at 5.67 YPA on 48 attempts, and they blitz only 14% so the matchup is linebackers and safeties, not outside corners. Jacksonville is sound vs the run at 3.79 YPC but soft in the middle at 14.45 YPA on 11 attempts and has allowed 13 explosives on 92 passes.
injury_fallout: No injuries were saved for JAX at CIN, so there is no injury fallout to price and usage stays with Tuten's 43 carries, Parker Washington's 23 targets, Higgins' 23 targets, and Ja'Marr Chase's 25 targets.
qb_vs_blitz: Trevor Lawrence is -0.23 EPA/dropback vs blitz (n=25) but +0.45 with no blitz, and Cincinnati's 14% blitz rate keeps him in the good split. Joe Burrow is -0.31 vs blitz (n=36) and +0.32 without, and Jacksonville's 32% blitz rate puts about a third of his dropbacks in the bad split, which funnels Cincinnati's passing value to Higgins' 302 air yards rather than a clean Burrow rhythm game.

picks.why: Tuten is at 68.0 rush yards per game (204 on 43 carries, 4.74 YPC) and Cincinnati has allowed 5.00 YPC plus 8 runs of 10+, so 57.5 sits under both his L3 average and this front; Cincinnati blitzes only 14%, so Jacksonville is not forced off the Tuten workload.

Higgins has 244 yards on 23 targets (81.3 per game) and 302 air yards, 19 yards per game above 62.5, and Jacksonville has allowed 13 passes of 20+ on 92 attempts with 14.45 YPA in the middle; even with Burrow at -0.31 EPA vs a 32% blitz, 68% of dropbacks are the +0.32 no-blitz split where Higgins has already outproduced Chase's 185 yards on 25 targets.
